title: Exponentiation and morphism-space lifting for isofibrations
statement:
Use the simplicial sets, inner horns, equivalence edges and quasicategories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A degreewise injective map is a simplicial map whose map in every simplicial degree is injective. An inner fibration is a simplicial map with the right lifting property against every inner horn inclusion $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $0<i<n$. An isofibration between quasicategories is an inner fibration $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ such that every equivalence edge $e:p(c)\to d$ lifts to an equivalence edge $\widetilde e:c\to\widetilde d$ with $p(\widetilde e)=e$. A Kan fibration is a simplicial map with the right lifting property against all horn inclusions, including the two outer horns, in dimensions at least one. For an isofibration $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and any degreewise injective map $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ of small simplicial sets, the exponential corner map
$$\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal C)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal C)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal D)}\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal D)$$
is an isofibration between quasicategories. In particular $\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal C)$ is an isofibration for every quasicategory $\mathcal C$. For a quasicategory $\mathcal C$ and vertices $x,y$, set
$$U_{\mathcal C}(x,y)=\{x\}\times_{\mathcal C,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,\mathcal C}\{y\}.$$
For any inner fibration $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between quasicategories, the induced map $U_{\mathcal C}(x,y)\to U_{\mathcal D}(p(x),p(y))$ is a Kan fibration between Kan complexes.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.5.1 (Kerodon Tag 01F1), Corollary 4.4.5.3 (01F3), and Proposition 4.6.1.22 (01P8), the last for the unpinched U mapping spaces. These are Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags. Read online 2026-10-16; WANTED: archived source.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-inner-fibration-corner] to any inner fibration $r:E\to F$ and the given degreewise injection $i:A\to B$: the corner map is an inner fibration. This is the product/internal-hom lifting argument formerly written inline. For $r:X\to\Delta^0$ and $i:\varnothing\hookrightarrow H$ its target is a point, so $\operatorname{Fun}(H,X)$ is a quasicategory whenever $X$ is. For $r:\mathcal D\to\Delta^0$ and arbitrary $i$, the same lemma says that restriction $\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal D)$ is an inner fibration. Its pullback target $T=\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal C)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal D)}\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal D)$ is a quasicategory: project an inner horn to the first factor, fill it there, then lift its image filler through the restriction inner fibration in the second factor. Pairing the two fillers satisfies the pullback equation. The source $\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal C)$ is a quasicategory by the preceding empty-shape specialization.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.5.1, inner-fibration and quasicategory part, expanded by the lifting adjunction and the existing inner-anodyne pushout-product theorem (compare Proposition 4.1.4.1).

proof.text: Let $u:B\to\mathcal C$ be an object and let $\tau$ be an equivalence edge in $T$ starting at the image of $u$. The two projections of $\tau$ give maps $\Delta^1\times A\to\mathcal C$ and $g:\Delta^1\times B\to\mathcal D$, compatible over $A$, with initial maps $u|_A$ and $pu$. Evaluating a simplicial functor on an equivalence preserves its inverse edge and its two witnessing triangles; hence all their vertex components are equivalences. For each vertex $b\in B$ outside $A$, use the isofibration hypothesis on $p$ to choose an equivalence edge $e_b$ starting at $u(b)$ and mapping exactly to $g|_{\Delta^1\times\{b\}}$. Let $A'=A\cup\operatorname{sk}_0B$, where $\operatorname{sk}_0B$ consists of the vertices and all their degeneracies. Glue the map on $\Delta^1\times A$, the edges $e_b$ with their degeneracies, and $u$ on $\{0\}\times B$. They agree on every intersection (at a new vertex the intersection is its specified initial object), so the pushout property in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $h_0:(\Delta^1\times A')\amalg_{\{0\}\times A'}(\{0\}\times B)\to\mathcal C$ over $g$. Now $A'$ contains every vertex of $B$, and every prescribed vertex edge is an equivalence. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-equivalence-prism-extension] with $r=p$ and $\epsilon=0$ to extend $h_0$ over $\Delta^1\times B$, still exactly over $g$. All vertex components remain the prescribed equivalences. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] this is an equivalence edge in $\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal C)$. Its initial endpoint is $u$ and its corner image is exactly $\tau$. Together with Step 1 this proves the asserted isofibration.

source.place: Corollary 4.4.5.9, adjoining the 0-skeleton and applying Proposition 4.4.5.8; the source-fixed version is obtained by opposites. The item uses the source-fixed definition of isofibration.

proof.text: The map $\mathcal C\to\Delta^0$ is an isofibration: inner lifting is the quasicategory condition, and the unique equivalence edge of the point lifts at any chosen $c$ to the degenerate identity edge of $c$ with degenerate inverse witnesses. Apply Steps 1-2 to this map. The two internal functor simplicial sets into $\Delta^0$ have exactly one simplex in each degree, so its corner target identifies degreewise with $\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal C)$. This gives the stated restriction isofibration, also for empty $A$ or $B$.

source.place: Corollary 4.4.5.3, specialization to the point; the point and identity-edge checks are explicit.

proof.text: Now assume only that $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ is an inner fibration, and fix $x,y$. Set $B=\Delta^1$, $A=\partial\Delta^1$ and $f:A\to\mathcal C$ with values $x,y$. The corner $\theta$ for $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ and $p$ is an inner fibration by Step 1. Pull it back along $v\mapsto(f,v)$ from $U_{\mathcal D}(p(x),p(y))$. Degreewise, the resulting source imposes exactly the two constant-endpoint equations defining $U_{\mathcal C}(x,y)$. A lifting square for this pullback maps to one for $\theta$; pair its filler with the specified base simplex. Thus $s:U_{\mathcal C}(x,y)\to U_{\mathcal D}(p(x),p(y))$ is an inner fibration. The boundary $A$ contains both vertices of $B$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-fixed-boundary-functor-kan] to $(X,f)=(\mathcal C,f)$ and $(\mathcal D,pf)$. The two strict fibers in that node are degreewise exactly these $U$ spaces, so both are Kan complexes, including when empty. The extracted lemma carries the previous fixed-boundary outer-horn and opposite-involution argument, without a pinch comparison.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.1.11, fixed-boundary Kan property, and the pullback identification from Proposition 4.6.1.24 (01PC). The retained direct prism/opposites route is assigned to the new fixed-boundary node.

proof.text: For a vertex $a\in U_{\mathcal C}(x,y)$ and an edge $\gamma$ in $U_{\mathcal D}(p(x),p(y))$ starting at $s(a)$, transpose $\gamma$ to $g:\Delta^1\times B\to\mathcal D$ with $B=\Delta^1$ as in Step 4. Its restriction to $\Delta^1\times A$ is constant at the two endpoint objects. Prescribe $h_0$ to be constant at $x,y$ on these two strips and to equal $a$ on $\{0\}\times B$. The overlaps agree, and $ph_0=g$ there; the gluing has exactly the pushout meaning of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The subset $A=\partial\Delta^1$ contains every vertex of $B$, and the two vertical edges of $h_0$ are identities, hence equivalences. Therefore [lem-coef-infinity-equivalence-prism-extension] with $\epsilon=0$ and this inner fibration $p$ gives an extension over the whole square. It is an edge in $U_{\mathcal C}(x,y)$ starting at $a$ and mapping exactly to $\gamma$. In particular it lifts every equivalence edge of the target. Every edge in the source Kan complex is itself an equivalence by the Kan-complex clause of [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration]. Hence $s$ is an isofibration between Kan complexes, using Step 4 for inner lifting. Apply the core-map clause of that same node to $s$: it gives a Kan fibration on cores. Its Kan-complex clause identifies both cores with the entire $U$ spaces, so this is precisely the asserted Kan fibration $U_{\mathcal C}(x,y)\to U_{\mathcal D}(p(x),p(y))$. This proves all horn lifts, including dimension one and both outer horns, without imposing equivalence lifting on the original $p$.
